recipe: React 19.2+: to keep hidden UI's state or pre-render likely-next UI, replace `{isVisible && <Page />}` with `<Activity mode={isVisible ? 'visible' : 'hidden'}><Page /></Activity>`. Hidden mode hides children, unmounts effects and defers updates.
trigger_condition: You want to hide part of the UI while preserving its state or pre-rendering it in the background.
evidence: You can use Activity as an alternative to conditionally rendering parts of your app:
_original_recipe: Replace conditional rendering with `<Activity>` when you want to pre-render hidden parts of your app without impacting the performance of visible content.
_review_reason: add version, syntax and hidden-mode semantics; Activity is not a blanket replacement for conditional rendering

recipe: React 19.2+: use `useEffectEvent` to split event logic out of an Effect when a value read only by that logic (e.g. theme) would otherwise make the Effect re-run.
trigger_condition: When you have an effect that handles external events and some values used in the event handler are unrelated to the effect's setup logic.
evidence: With `useEffectEvent`, you can split the "event" part of this logic out of the Effect that emits it:
_original_recipe: Use `useEffectEvent` to split event-handling logic out of `useEffect` when a prop or state value used only in the event handler would otherwise cause the effect to re-run unnecessarily.
_review_reason: missing version qualifier (useEffectEvent is new in 19.2)

recipe: Do not declare Effect Events in the dependency array, and upgrade to `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@latest` so the linter doesn't try to insert them as dependencies.
trigger_condition: When using `useEffectEvent` in a component or hook.
evidence: Effect Events should _not_ be declared in the dependency array**. You'll need to upgrade to `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@latest` so that the linter doesn't try to insert them as dependencies.

recipe: Use `useEffectEvent` only for functions that are conceptually "events" fired from an Effect, not to silence lint errors or wrap everything, as this can lead to bugs.
trigger_condition: When deciding whether to wrap a function in `useEffectEvent` or just disable a lint rule.
evidence: You should use `useEffectEvent` for functions that are conceptually "events" that happen to be fired from an Effect instead of a user event (that's what makes it an "Effect Event"). You don't need to wrap everything in `useEffectEvent`, or to use it just to silence the lint error, as this can lead to bugs.

recipe: React 19.2+, Server Components only: pass `cacheSignal()` as a fetch's `signal` (e.g. `dedupedFetch(url, { signal: cacheSignal() })` with `dedupedFetch = cache(fetch)`) so the work aborts when the `cache()` lifetime ends.
trigger_condition: When using React Server Components with `cache()` and you need to know when the cache lifetime ends to abort or clean up work.
evidence: `cacheSignal` allows you to know when the [`cache()`](/reference/react/cache) lifetime is over:
_original_recipe: Pass `cacheSignal()` as the signal to `fetch` inside a `cache()`-wrapped function to clean up or abort work when the cached result will no longer be used.
_review_reason: cacheSignal is RSC-only and is called in the component, not inside the cache()-wrapped function; add version

recipe: Use the new React Performance Tracks in Chrome DevTools to inspect the Scheduler and Components tracks when debugging how React splits your code into priorities or when components are rendered.
trigger_condition: When you need to understand how React splits your code into different priorities or identify performance problems in component rendering.
evidence: React 19.2 adds a new set of [custom tracks](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance/extension) to Chrome DevTools performance profiles to provide more information about the performance of your React app:
_review_reason: profiling tool, not a UI component

recipe: React 19.2+ Partial Pre-rendering: `const {prelude, postponed} = await prerender(<App />, {signal: controller.signal})` (react-dom/static), save `postponed`, serve `prelude` from a CDN, then `resume(<App />, postponed)` (react-dom/server) to stream dynamic content.
trigger_condition: When you want to pre-render static parts of your app and serve them from a CDN before resuming rendering with dynamic content.
evidence: This feature is called "Partial Pre-rendering", and allows you to pre-render the static parts of your app and serve it from a CDN, and then resume rendering the shell to fill it in with dynamic content later.
_original_recipe: Call `prerender` with an `AbortController` to pre-render static parts of your app, save the postponed state, send the prelude to a CDN, and later call `resume` to fill in dynamic content.

recipe: For SSR in Node.js use the Node Streams APIs (renderToPipeableStream, resumeToPipeableStream, prerenderToNodeStream, resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream): they are much faster than Web Streams in Node, and Web Streams lack compression by default.
trigger_condition: When implementing server-side rendering in a Node.js environment.
evidence: In Node.js environments, we still highly recommend using the Node Streams APIs:
_original_recipe: Use Node Streams APIs (renderToPipeableStream, resumeToPipeableStream, prerenderToNodeStream, resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream) instead of Web Streams for server-side rendering in Node.js, since Node Streams are much faster and support compression by default.
_review_reason: compression claim was inverted: the source says Web Streams lack compression by default
